name: Maximum-Parent Profiles under Constant Coordinates
statement: For nonempty proper $C\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$, $|X|=n$, and $t\ge1$, one has $\mathcal F(C\times\{0\}^t)=\{(r,s):s\ge n+t-1,\ (r,s-t)\in\mathcal F(C)\}$. Its minimal frontier is obtained from $(r,u)$ by $(r,\max(u+t,n+t-1))$ and deleting dominated points. Moreover $a(C\times\{0\}^t)=\min_{(r,u)\in\mathcal F(C)}\max\{r,r+u+1-n\}$, independent of positive $t$.
proof: Projecting constant visible coordinates from a parent gives necessity, while the complementary target contains an $(n+t-1)$-cube. Conversely, after raising the complementary rank if needed, use face avoidance to choose a rank-one-lower maximum subclass avoiding the mark and lift it beneath the parent at the new constant coordinate. This preserves rank and auxiliary count while raising complementary rank by one; iterate and translate the frontier formula.
